newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Illovo, Tongaat mills hit by strike.
newsitem.headline: Illovo, Tongaat mills hit by strike.

text.p: A wage strike by 4,000 sugar workers from five unions has halted operations at 14 mills of South African firms Tongaat-Hulett Ltd and Illovo Sugar Ltd since midnight on Tuesday, officials said on Wednesday.
A sugar industry source said while the strike was legal, protesting workers would be locked out of mills and refineries from 1600 GMT on Wednesday.
A Food and Allied Workers Union official at a refinery in Rossburgh, near Durban, said workers were demanding a 20 percent increase, but the industry was offering only 10.5 percent.

"We are demanding 20 percent across the board, but that does not mean we are inflexible...if they (the companies) come with something reasonable we may settle," Anthony Zulu, a local union chairman told Reuters.
He declined to give a specific figure.
The sugar industry source said all milling operations in KwaZulu-Natal had been affected, but would not say by how much production was being hit.
The strike has come as sugar cane is being harvested and milled.
The official spokesmen for the two companies could not be reached for comment. --Durban Newsroom, +27 31 306 8646
